items.title: Pre-season: Newcastle vs Everton team news LIVE!
O'Sullivan's poor start to season continues with early China Open loss
items.description: Ronnie O'Sullivan's poor start to the new season continued after he lost 6-4 to Noppon Saengkham in the second round of the China Open.

items.title: Lakers to be sold in record-breaking £9bn deal
items.description: The Los Angeles Lakers are set to be sold for a record-breaking $12.5bn (£9.25bn) to Josh Kushner, the venture capitalist who was at the centre of FIFA's proposed new commercial structure.

items.title: Arsenal reignite interest in Aston Villa's Konsa
items.description: Aston Villa's central defender Ezri Konsa is thought to be Arsenal's preferred option in their search for a new central defender.

items.title: Cadillac sack team principal Lowdon as Budkowski takes charge
items.description: Cadillac have sacked team principal Graeme Lowdon and replaced him with Marcin Budkowski in what Formula 1's 2026 newcomers claim is a "planned leadership transition".

items.title: Messi hints at retirement in tribute to late father
items.description: Lionel Messi has admitted he has doubts over whether he will continue his playing career following the death of his father, Jorge, saying, "I don't know how to carry on."

items.title: Rangers seek striker & are 'playing with fire' in defence
items.description: Rangers are being "proactive" in seeking a new striker after Youssef Chermiti was ruled out long term, says manager Derek McInnes, who warns defensive injuries leave the club "playing with fire".

items.title: Coles and Opoku-Fordjour among 25 England players given enhanced contracts
items.description: Alex Coles and Asher Opoku-Fordjour are among five England players to be awarded an enhanced contract by the RFU for the first time.

items.title: Palace bid for Monaco midfielder Camara rejected
items.description: Ligue 1 side Monaco reject Crystal Palace's verbal bid for midfielder Lamine Camara.

items.title: Draper in line to meet Djokovic at Cincinnati Open
Fery feels 'no added pressure' despite being British No 1 as he returns
items.description: Arthur Fery insists he feels “no added pressure” as the new British No 1 prepares to return to action this weekend for the first time since his memorable run to the Wimbledon semi-finals.
